title: Bi-temporal Image-driven Acute Stroke Evolution Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2602.07535v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Acute ischemic stroke requires rapid treatment decisions that are strongly guided by emergency imaging. Admission computed tomography perfusion (CTP) is commonly used to estimate the ischemic core, representing irreversibly damaged tissue, and the penumbra, representing hypoperfused but potentially salvageable tissue. Follow-up diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) is then used to define the final infarct. Existing imaging approaches primarily focus on core--penumbra segmentation or final-infarct prediction, but provide limited insight into how heterogeneous penumbral tissue evolves after treatment. We propose a bi-temporal tissue phenotyping framework that links admission CTP signatures with follow-up DWI-defined tissue outcome using six outcome-aware region-of-interest classes. translated_title: 双时相影像驱动的急性脑卒中演变分析
translated_abstract: 急性缺血性脑卒中需要快速的治疗决策，而急诊影像学检查对这些决策具有重要的指导作用。入院时的CT灌注成像（CTP）通常用于评估缺血核心（代表不可逆损伤的组织）和缺血半暗带（代表低灌注但具有潜在挽救价值的组织）。随后，随访的弥散加权磁共振成像（DWI）被用于界定最终梗死灶。现有的影像学方法主要聚焦于核心-半暗带分割或最终梗死预测，但对于异质性的半暗带组织在治疗后如何演变，所提供的见解十分有限。我们提出了一种双时相组织表型分析框架，利用六种基于结局的兴趣区类别，将入院时CTP影像特征与随访DWI所界定的组织结局联系起来。入院时的组织特征通过从mJ-Net和nnU-Net表征中提取的统计特征、影像组学特征以及深度学习特征来进行刻画。
tldr: 本文提出一种双时相组织表型分析框架，利用六种结局感知的兴趣区类别将入院CTP影像特征与随访DWI组织结局相关联，从而揭示治疗后半暗带组织的异质性演变过程。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a bi-temporal tissue phenotyping framework that links admission CTP signatures with follow-up DWI-defined tissue outcomes through six outcome-aware region-of-interest classes, revealing the heterogeneous evolution of penumbral tissue after treatment.
